model_type: sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline (SimpleImputer[median] -> StandardScaler -> Lasso), predicts DELTA, trained on real + noise-augmented data (matching src/data/augment_ila.py's exact noise model)
target_description: The CHANGE (drift) in the instrument's reference value between the current measurement and its next calibration/verification campaign. The API reconstructs and returns the absolute predicted next value (valeur_reference + predicted_delta).
prediction_unit: UNKNOWN / REQUIRES CONFIRMATION - not recorded in the source ILA data. 'valeur_reference' is instrument-category dependent (see reports/data_dictionary/Data_Dictionary.xlsx).

feature_notes.recent_shift: (valeur_reference - ewm_mean) / (EMT_haute - EMT_basse) - THE ONLY FEATURE WITH A NON-ZERO COEFFICIENT (-0.485). Captures regression-to-the-mean: when the current reading is above its own recent historical average, the model predicts a corresponding downward correction, and vice versa.

why_augmentation_helps_here: A real, statistically significant regression-to-the-mean pattern exists in the real data alone (recent_shift vs target_delta: Pearson r=-0.368, p<0.000001, n=624 real training rows) - but Lasso cannot confidently assign it a non-zero coefficient from only ~36 rows/instrument (verified directly: real-only training collapses to all-zero coefficients, the same failure mode found in v2). Augmentation adds ~1100 additional (X,y) pairs built by perturbing each real row's CURRENT reading with noise ~ N(0, incertitude) - the instrument's own measurement uncertainty, using the exact same noise model as src/data/augment_ila.py - while holding its real historical features (ewm_mean, rolling stats) and its real future outcome (target_next_valeur_reference) fixed. This reinforces the SAME real, pre-existing pattern rather than inventing a new one, letting the regularized model detect and use it with confidence.
preprocessing_description: The saved artifact is a single scikit-learn Pipeline (SimpleImputer[median] -> StandardScaler -> Lasso) predicting the DELTA. The API computes the 5 normalized features server-side from the same 12 raw physical inputs the metrologist already enters (no UI/schema change). Training data: 741 real rows + 1,386 noise-augmented rows (3 augmented copies per real row, using each row's own recorded measurement uncertainty).
training_dataset: data/processed/ILA_features_selected.csv + data/processed/ILA_cleaned.csv (for incertitude) + augmentation via src/data/augment_ila.py's noise model, applied consistently in train_v3_augmented.py
cv_strategy_reference: GroupKFold (grouped by id_instrument, 5 folds). Augmentation is generated separately for each fold's training portion only (never leaking into the held-out test fold), and the alpha search itself is honest (evaluated via the same held-out folds, not a separate optimistic split).

evaluation_metrics_chronological_referen.note: Computed via train_v3_augmented.py's chronological check (train on years <= 2024, test on years > 2024). Provided as a secondary reference point; GroupKFold is the primary reported metric for this model card, matching v1/v2 convention.

known_limitations: IMPORTANT: this model does NOT beat the trivial persistence baseline under either validation strategy (GroupKFold: 2.120 vs baseline 1.957; chronological: 0.739 vs baseline 0.522). It is the closest of any approach tested in this project, and should be described that way - not as 'beating' the baseline.

UNLIKE v1 and v2, this model has a real, non-zero, interpretable coefficient: recent_shift = -0.485. This reflects a genuine, statistically verified regression-to-the-mean pattern present in the real (non-augmented) data alone (Pearson r=-0.368, p<0.000001, n=624) - augmentation stabilized detection of this pre-existing signal rather than inventing one. See why_augmentation_helps_here above.

Augmentation is NOT a substitute for more real calibration data. The improvement comes from more confidently detecting an already-present but statistically noisy real pattern, not from creating new information. It cannot close the remaining gap to baseline, which the audit's other experiments (subset restriction to well-documented instruments) attribute to insufficient real history per instrument.

The other 4 features (pos_in_band, ewm_pos_in_band, rolling_trend, uncertainty_norm) all have zero coefficients - they do not contribute to this model's predictions. Only recent_shift and the intercept are used.

R-squared is inflated and should not be trusted alone: instrument scales vary from -24 to 553, so any predictor that gets roughly the right scale regime achieves R2 > 0.9 regardless of genuine drift-prediction skill. MAE against baseline is the trustworthy metric.

No scientifically validated drift threshold exists. The API and UI must never label a prediction 'safe', 'critical', or 'dangerous' - only 'prediction generated' or the baseline-first recommendation, with a neutral, factual interpretation.
This tool is a decision-support aid. It must never automatically replace a metrologist's professional judgement, and does not by itself constitute ISO/IEC 17025 evidence of conformity.

See AUDIT_REPORT.md and experiments/audit_v3/FINAL_REPORT.md for the full audit trail, including the v1 (collinear features) -> v2 (normalized features, zero coefficients) -> v3 (augmented, non-zero coefficient) progression.
